values.note: 80 modern sites (most back-in) and 20 rustic non-electric back-in sites; every one posts a pad of 38 ft or more. Sewer only at four modern sites (M16, M17, M19, M21).

sites.source: Washington County camping page ('Eighty campsites, suited for tents, trailers, or motor homes. Most sites are back-in.'; 'Twenty spacious non-electric back-in sites.') + booking site grid (Modern 80 units, pads 38-142 ft; Rustic 20 units, pads 40-59 ft), read 2026-11-11

facilities.source: Washington County camping page (Modern: 'Modern bathroom facilities with flush toilets and hot showers.', 'Trailer/RV dump station.'; Rustic: 'Vault or portable toilets available.'; rate table 'Dump Station (included with camping reservation) $15'), read 2026-11-11

values.note: 2026 season April 24 to October 17; the booking site has 2027 loaded from April 30 to October 23. Closed from the end of October to the end of April.

season.source: Washington County camping page ('The 2026 campground season begins Friday, April 24 and ends Saturday, October 17, 2026.'; 'Washington County Campgrounds are closed annually between the end of October to the end of April.') + booking site grid for facility 32 (in season 2027-04-30 to 2027-10-23), read 2026-11-11

values.note: Book online or through the park office. The 14-night limit counts any 30-day period. All campers register at the park office; the gate closes at 10 p.m. (code from the office).

booking.source: Washington County camping page ('Campsite reservations will open 120 days before the campers' desired arrival date.'; 'Weekends: 2-night minimum stay (Friday and Saturday).'; 'Holiday weekends: 3-night minimum stay.'; '14-day maximum stay at any Washington County campground in any 30-day period.'; 'All campers must register at the Park Office.') + booking site restrictions (MaximumStay 14), read 2026-11-11

values.note: Rustic (no electric) $30 a night, 20/30-amp $35, 50-amp with water $45, 50-amp with water and sewer $50; $6 off every site in October. One camping unit a site; extra vehicles park in the overflow lot.

note: Washington County park reserve. The modern campground's loops sit in open grassland and scattered trees north of the park's lakes, beside a small pond; a sand-bottom swim pond is nearby. Horses are allowed at the rustic sites. No pets. --Claude
summary: County page + every booking-site unit read: 80 modern (50-amp/water at 1-58, four web-bookable sewer sites) + 20 rustic sites, all pads 38 ft+; $30 rustic / $35 / $45 / $50, $6 off in October (low 35 -> 24 with seasonal spans), $8 reservation fee, $7 vehicle permit; 2026 season Apr 24-Oct 17 (2027 loaded Apr 30-Oct 23); 120-day window, weekend 2 / holiday 3-night minimums, 14-night max. Electric 30 -> 50, sewer false -> true. Pin ~380 m off; not waterfront kept.
flags: Pin: stored 44.98480,-92.89560 is on the park road/parking area north of the campground, ~380 m from the modern campground (booking-site facility point 44.98144,-92.89639, which sits inside the loops on imagery). Suggest 44.9815,-92.8964.

Hookups: sewer false -> true on four web-bookable sites (M16, M17, M19, M21, '50 Amp Electric/Water/Sewer', $50). The county page says 'Camp host sites include sewer hookup', so these may be host pads released to the public; they are offered online to anyone, so they count.

Fees: nightly_low 35 -> 24. The rustic non-electric sites ($30, back-in, pads 40-59 ft on the booking site) take a motorhome, and October is $6 off, so the cheapest real night is $24 (October rustic); seasonal spans carry the main-season $30-50. Rustic sites allow horses ('Horses allowed at each campsite').

Waterfront: not waterfront kept. On imagery the modern loops sit in grassland/trees with a small pond (~1 ha, under 5 acres = a pond) at the east loop; Eagle Point Lake and Lake Elmo are 300 m+ south and west behind woods.
Pets are not allowed in the campgrounds (county policy) - a usability note for the reviewer, kept in the entry note.
